resale_co.name: Certificate of Inspection Permitting Occupancy (Borough code, Building and Housing chapter)
resale_co.issued_by: Borough Construction Official or his agent (per the Borough code); the Borough's construction code is enforced by the NJ DCA Northern Regional Office
requirements: Apply in writing to the Construction Official before the rental, transfer of title or occupancy of any dwelling house or dwelling unit
Inspection for compliance with all Borough ordinances, rules and regulations on use and occupancy of dwellings
Title may transfer after the application is filed, but no one may occupy the home until all items marked for correction are completed
Owner or agent must give a reasonable time for the inspection and have someone present to provide entry

fees.label: Certificate of inspection permitting occupancy
fees.quote: The fee for issuance of such certificate as provided for herein shall be $50.

resale_co.how_to_apply: The Borough code says to apply in writing to the Construction Official. The Borough website gives no application form or process for this certificate, and construction code services are run by the NJ DCA Northern Regional Office (NRO.inspectionrequests@dca.nj.gov, 908-713-0722). Call the Borough office at 973-827-3444 to confirm who handles it and how to apply.

evidence.quote: Transfers of title may take place after application of a certificate of inspection for occupancy

Prior to the rental, transfer of title or occupancy of any dwelling house or houses or any dwelling unit or units provided for in this section, application for certificate of inspection permitting occupancy shall be made in writing to the Construction Official or his agent of the Borough

hereby relinquishes its jurisdiction of the administration and enforcement of the Uniform Construction Code and hereby transfers jurisdiction for the administration and enforcement of the Uniform Construction Code to the Department of Community Affairs of the State of New Jersey.
All inspections requests must be made in writing by scanning the QR for the form site or following the link below.
Zoning Officer/Code Enforcement Officer Joseph Setticase

resale_co.notes: Borough code Section 11-5 (1976 Code Section 8-1.11, Ord. No. 5-88), read through the ecode360 library, requires a certificate of inspection permitting occupancy from the Construction Official before any transfer of title, rental or new occupancy of a dwelling, and makes real estate brokers and agents who take part in a violating transaction liable too. In 2012 (Ord. No. 1-12) the Borough handed construction code enforcement to the NJ DCA, and the Borough website does not mention this certificate, so it is unclear whether it is still issued or who issues it. Marked required because the code says so, with medium confidence; confirm by phone. The Zoning Officer's hours are Saturday 8 AM to 10 AM by appointment (email zoning@ogdensburgnj.gov).

requirements: Smoke detector on each level of the dwelling, including basements, excluding attic or crawl space (DCA form)
Smoke detector and carbon monoxide alarm outside each separate sleeping area, within 10 feet of bedrooms (DCA form)
All smoke detectors and CO alarms in working order; AC powered or interconnected alarms in homes built after January 1977 must be kept working (DCA form)
Fire extinguisher (form still lists it; dropped from the state requirement in February 2025 by P.L.2025, c.19)

authorities.name: NJ Department of Community Affairs, Division of Fire Safety, Bureau of Fire Code Enforcement (state-enforced; State LEA for Ogdensburg)
authorities.lead_time: State fee tiers count business days between the Division's receipt and the closing date: more than ten business days for the lowest fee. If the change of occupant does not happen within 6 months, a new application is needed (per the DCA form).

fees.label: State smoke/CO certificate (N.J.A.C. 5:70-2.9(d)), received more than 10 business days before the change of occupant
fees.quote: Requests for a CSACMAPFEC received more than 10 business days prior to the change of occupant: $45.00

fees.label: Received four to 10 business days before
fees.quote: Requests for a CSACMAPFEC received four to 10 business days prior to the change of occupant: $90.00

fees.label: Received fewer than four business days before
fees.quote: Requests for a CSACMAPFEC received fewer than four business days prior to the change of occupant: $161.00

authorities.how_to_apply: Apply online through the NJ DCA Fire Safety Service Portal (firesolutions.dca.nj.gov): choose Apply for an Application, then Apply for Smoke Certification, fill in the data and pay. Help: BFCECodeAdmin@dca.nj.gov or 609-633-6132. The older DCA paper form goes to PO Box 809, Trenton, NJ 08625-0809 with a check payable to Treasurer, State of New Jersey.

fire_cert.notes: Ogdensburg is state-enforced (LEA code S), so the smoke/CO certificate comes from the NJ Division of Fire Safety, not the Borough; the Borough fire chapter and website say nothing about it. The state directory entry is old (survey 2/1/2019) and lists the smoke compliance office as the Ogdensburg Building Department, 14 Highland Avenue, (973) 827-3860, which may be outdated. The only state fee schedule found is on the DCA paper form (revised 10/02), which may be out of date; the portal does not publish fees publicly. That form still lists a fire extinguisher, which state law (P.L.2025, c.19) removed in February 2025. Confirm current fees and process with the Division of Fire Safety. Update: the current state fees are $45 / $90 / $161, set by N.J.A.C. 5:70-2.9(d) (50 N.J.R. 729(a)) (more than 10, 4 to 10, and under 4 business days before closing). The $35 / $70 / $125 on the older DCA paper form are out of date.

other_items.label: Final water reading
other_items.detail: The Borough Water Billing Department (973-827-3444 x2) needs a Final Water Reading Request with the exact closing date, the seller's attorney contact and the buyer's name (required to move the account to the buyer). Call if the closing date changes or is cancelled. No fee is shown on the form.

open_questions: Is the Borough's certificate of inspection permitting occupancy (Section 11-5, $50) still issued on resales, and by whom (NJ DCA Northern Regional Office or a Borough code officer)?
What is the current state fee for a smoke/CO certificate through the DCA portal, and the usual lead time for a state inspection in Ogdensburg?
Does the Borough Building Department (14 Highland Avenue) still take smoke certificate requests as the old state directory says?
